items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines -September 18, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Granted Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has been granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence on condition that he pays the RM50 million fine imposed over his conviction in the SRC International case. Security measures Police have tightened security measures across Negri Sembilan following developments concerning the state's royal institution. Penalties Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak and his family face more than RM21 billion in fines, tax claims, civil judgments and other court-imposed financial orders arising from several criminal, tax and civil cases .

items.title: Wawasan: Najib's conditional pardon must be respected by all parties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) has welcomed the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, saying the decision by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, should be respected by all parties. Wawasan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah said the decision had brought an end to the controversy surrounding Najib's pardon and expressed appreciation to Sultan Ibrahim for resolving the matter. "The Article 42(1) of the Federal Constitution provided the King with the power to grant pardons, reprieves and respites.

items.title: Nearly 1 in 4 doctors worldwide approaching retirement age
items.summary: The finding, based on the latest available data from 122 countries, was published in WHO's new report on global health workforce levels and trends. "Ageing is the hidden health workforce crisis that requires urgent attention," said Khassoum Diallo, acting head of WHO's health workforce policies and data unit. WHO projects a global shortage of 11.1 million health workers by 2030, with 67 countries expected to lack enough personnel to meet their populations' health needs.

items.title: Pakatan backs PM’s stance on Najib pardon, says no one is above the law
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) today backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s stance and the advice given by the Attorney General and Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional royal pardon. In a statement issued after the Pardons Board meeting earlier today, the PH Presidential Council said it firmly stood with the Prime Minister’s position and the advice given to the board. Anwar earlier said the conditional royal pardon did not weaken the government’s resolve to fight corruption.

items.title: PH: No one above law, convicted offenders must serve sentences
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council today stressed that no one is above the law and that anyone convicted of an offence must serve their sentence in accordance with the Federal Constitution and the law. In a statement issued after its meeting today, the council said it stood firmly behind Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's position, as well as the advice given by the Attorney-General and Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board. "The PH Presidential Council firmly stands with the position of the prime minister, as well as the advice given by the Attorney-General and the Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board today," it said.

items.title: Perak, Melaka, Johor Umno back Najib solidarity fund
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno leaders in Perak, Melaka and Johor have welcomed the party's initiative to raise funds to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak settle his RM50 million fine. Perak Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the state chapter was grateful for the Pardons Board's decision to grant Najib a conditional pardon. He also welcomed Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's initiative to launch a contribution fund to help Najib settle the RM50 million fine.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, Sept 18, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1535714]] [[nid:1535713]] [[nid:1535712]] [[nid:1535711]] [[nid:1535710]] [[nid:1535709]] [[nid:1535708]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against greenback on easing oil supply concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar and other major currencies at Friday's close, buoyed by improved market sentiment following easing concerns over crude oil supply, an analyst said. At 6pm, the local currency rose to 4.0795/0840 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0965/1010. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude prices fell on expectations of improving conditions in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: ES Sunlogy wins Parkland Southern contract in Johor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ES Sunlogy Bhd's wholly-owned Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd has secured a RM15.6 million contract from Parkland Southern Sdn Bhd for electrical works at a development in Johor. The development comprises two 29-storey serviced apartment towers as well as a seven-storey podium featuring serviced apartments, recreational facilities, parking facilities and commercial space. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Carimin raises Sealink stake to 24.1pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Carimin Petroleum Bhd has increased its direct stake in Sealink International Bhd to 24.1 per cent. This followed the acquisition of 23 million Sealink shares via a direct business transaction. A Bursa Malaysia filing dated Sept 18 showed that Carimin's direct holdings rose to 120.5 million shares from 97.5 million previously.

items.title: Macau concludes first closed-door national security trial
items.summary: MACAU: Macau has concluded its first national security trial behind closed doors, a court said on Friday, days after proceedings began in a former pro-democracy lawmaker's case. A verdict will be issued at a later date, Macau's Court of First Instance said in a statement. The Chinese casino hub expanded the scope of national security laws in May 2023, and a bill passed this year allows judges to hear national security cases behind closed doors.

items.title: Malaysia, Australia move towards strategic defence collaboration - Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Australia have agreed to elevate their existing defence ties from cooperation to closer, more practical and strategic collaboration, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. He said the agreement was reached at the sixth Malaysia-Australia High-Level Committee (HLC) Meeting, which he co-chaired with Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles in Geelong, Australia today. Earlier, Khaled and Marles held a bilateral meeting before co-chairing the HLC meeting.

items.title: Pahang Sultan witnesses signing of wind turbine project agreement in Pekan
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah Al-Sultan Abdullah, witnessed the signing ceremony of a collaboration agreement to develop a wind turbine project in Pekan. Amat Bayu director Datuk Ahmad Najmi Abdul Razak, who signed the agreement on behalf of the company, said the event marked an important milestone for Amat Bayu and its UAE partners in developing the 2.2-megawatt wind turbine project in Tanjung Batu, Pekan. "This project is beyond the development of a single wind turbine, it is about taking the first step towards unlocking the potential of wind energy in Malaysia.

items.title: Jati Tinggi Group lands RM72.8mil data centre job, order book swells to RM1.1bil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd's wholly-owned Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd has secured a RM72.8 million contract for power infrastructure works linked to a data centre in Banting, Selangor. The project is scheduled for completion by Jan 15 next year, Tinggi Group said in a statement today. Managing director Datuk Wira Lim Yeong Seong said the latest award reflected growing opportunities in private-sector power infrastructure, particularly as data centres drive demand for medium- and high-voltage connections.

items.title: Capital A considers divesting Big Pay, Tune Protect stake as it restructures Move Digital to address RM292mil liabilities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Capital A Bhd is undertaking a court-supervised scheme of arrangement for its wholly-owned indirect subsidiary Move Digital Sdn Bhd, which could see the divestment of the latter's stake in Big Pay Pte Ltd, and Tune Protect Group Bhd. Move Digital is seeking an order to convene a meeting with its creditors and a three-month restraining order. The scheme creditors involved are primarily internal group entities, including Capital A itself, AirAsia SEA Sdn Bhd, AirAsia Move, Ikhlas Com Travel Sdn Bhd, Santan Food Sdn Bhd, AirAsia Bhd, and PT Indonesia AirAsia.

items.title: PH Presidential Council meeting ends after nearly two hours
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Pakatan Harapan Presidential Council meeting ended after nearly two hours tonight, amid heightened political developments surrounding Barisan Nasional's position in the Unity Government. The meeting, which began around 5.30pm, was understood to have been chaired by PH chairman and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The meeting comes amid renewed political attention following the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under conditional house arrest, subject to a RM50 million fine.

items.title: Jail and rotan for businessman who tricked director into paying over RM360,000 for AED supply
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A businessman was sentenced to 14 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to cheating a company director over a project to supply automated external defibrillator (AED) units. Judge Azrul Darus ordered Datuk Seri Azraie Jamaludin, 49, to serve the sentence from today. Azraie, together with another person still at large, was charged with deceiving Lim Wei Xiang, 35, into believing that he had the capacity to secure an AED supply project, which prompted Lim to deposit RM361,150 into the ZAJ Empire Resource bank account belonging to the accused.

items.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chair, becomes chairman emeritus
items.summary: NEW YORK: Berkshire Hathaway said on Friday that Warren Buffett will step down as the conglomerate's chairman and will become its chairman emeritus, effective immediately. The conglomerate named his son, Howard Buffett, a Berkshire director since 1993, as chairman. Buffett built Berkshire into an approximately US$1.03 trillion conglomerate with dozens of businesses, including Geico car insurance, the BNSF railroad, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, Dairy Queen ice cream, Fruit of the Loom underwear and Squishmallows plush toys.

items.title: 14 foreign motorists caught without valid licences within four hours
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Police seized 14 vehicles, including 11 motorcycles and three cars, during a four-hour special operation targeting foreign motorists here today. The vehicles were seized after their foreign drivers and riders were found to be operating without valid driving licences. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the operation, conducted by the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division from 7am to 10am, also saw 39 traffic summonses issued for various offences.

items.title: Girl with cerebral palsy in Shah Alam loses RM1m suit over school chair-pulling incident, family to appeal
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 18 — The High Court today dismissed a RM1 million civil suit filed by a teenage girl with cerebral palsy and her parents against six defendants over an incident in which she fell after another pupil allegedly pulled away a chair at a school here in 2023. Judicial Commissioner Datuk Anita Harun also ordered the plaintiffs to pay RM10,000 in costs, national news agency Bernama reported today. Earlier, Federal Senior Counsel Afiq Nazrin Zaharinan, representing all six defendants, sought RM30,000 in costs, while the plaintiffs’ lawyer, Sofian Azmir, sought RM10,000, before the Judicial Commissioner ordered the plaintiffs to pay RM10,000 in costs to all six defendants.

items.title: Rauf: Melaka to keep cutting protocol to give public direct access to leaders
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh says his administration will continue to do away with protocol in engagements with the people so they have direct access to state leaders. He said the approach allows leaders and officials to hear the people's concerns and complaints first-hand. Rauf said the initiative aligns with the "Melaka Sayang Rakyat" policy, which aims to simplify administrative procedures and cut red tape.

items.title: 'Mak Ton' found alone, covered in faeces at Ulu Tiram home
items.summary: ULU TIRAM: An elderly woman was found lying on the floor, covered in faeces, inside a squalid home where the electricity and water supplies had been cut off for months. The woman, known only as Mak Ton, was found inside her terrace house in Kampung Mawar here on Sept 12. Kampung Oren and Tebrau village chairman Johar Samat said neighbours became concerned after she was not seen outside her house for several days.

items.title: No sign of Najib's family at Langgak Duta residence as of 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: There was no sign of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's family members at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence as of 7pm today, hours after he was granted a conditional royal pardon. Checks at the residence found that members of the media and Najib's supporters remained gathered outside, awaiting further developments following the announcement earlier today. ](https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1535573/updated-najibs-special-officer-tight-lipped-media-wait-outside-jalan) Earlier today, Najib's special officer Ahmad Lutfi Azhar was seen arriving at his Langgak Duta residence, hours after he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

items.title: YTL Power lines up 5.2 GW gas build, US firms among potential off-takers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd is planning more than 5.25 gigawatts (GW) of new gas-fired power generation capacity across Malaysia and Southeast Asia, a major expansion driven by surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres. The expansion could increase YTL Power's total installed generation capacity to more than 11GW by 2030. One source said the planned power expansion was closely linked to YTL Power's strategic relationship with Nvidia, which has backed the group's AI cloud ambitions.

items.title: Civil servant arrested after faking theft of wife's Vellfire for insurance payout
items.summary: PADANG BESAR: A civil servant was arrested yesterday for faking the theft of his wife's Toyota Vellfire to claim an insurance payout. Padang Besar police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Shokri Abdullah said the 42-year-old suspect was detained alongside three other men. He said the suspects, aged between 32 and 45, were arrested in three separate raids around Padang Besar and Arau.

items.title: Najib's house arrest could hurt Malaysia's anti-graft credibility — TI-M
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest could have serious implications for Malaysia's anti-corruption credibility, said Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M). "It may also set expectations for similar treatment in future cases involving grand corruption and financial crime, potentially weakening the deterrent effect of Malaysia's anti-corruption framework," he said in a statement. He added that the case also had implications for Malaysia's international standing on the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) global ranking.

items.title: MCMC steps up social media monitoring as Melaka election preparations gather pace
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will continue monitoring social media content ahead of the Melaka state election and reminds internet users not to touch on 3R issues involving religion, race and royalty. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the monitoring was part of MCMC’s role as the regulator of the communications and multimedia sector, with the commission also working with other enforcement agencies when necessary. “MCMC, as the regulator, we will always monitor social media content.

items.title: Nearly 300 higher education sites now connected under nationwide Wi-Fi project
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 19 — The Public Higher Education Institution (IPTA) Wi-Fi project, covering 539 locations nationwide, is expected to be fully completed by September, with 55 per cent, or 294 locations, already having access to Wi-Fi, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said. She said the project covers 539 locations, involving IPTA and skills training institutions under Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) and the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma). Teo said Phases 1 and 2 of the project had been completed at 191 locations, with Phase 3 implementation now underway at institutions under Mara and Kesuma.

items.title: Perlis Umno launches solidarity fund for Najib
items.summary: ARAU: Perlis Umno today launched a state-level Datuk Seri Najib Razak Solidarity Fund to help the former prime minister settle the RM50 million fine which would allow him to serve his house arrest. Earlier today, Zahid said Umno is launching a fundraising bid to help Najib pay the RM50 million fine. Following that, Umno launched the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund.

items.title: TSR Capital secures RM158mil construction contract from PKNS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: TSR Capital Bhd has announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, TSR Bina Sdn Bhd, has secured a construction contract worth approximately RM158 million from Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Selangor (PKNS). The multi-million ringgit win is expected to deliver a steady boost to the group's bottom line over the medium term to the financial year ended June 30, 2029, according to its board of directors. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 18, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock KLCI index closed lower as investors remain cautious amid the Federal Reserve's hawkish stand which led to persistent foreign selling of the local market. The key index dropped nearly 10 points to close at 1,665. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin rose to RM319,480.

items.title: Stray dog-catcher probed over obscene gesture
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Police have recorded the statement of an animal management contractor stray dog-catcher over an alleged obscene and humiliating hand gesture towards a 29-year-old woman during an operation in Sri Gading here yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the woman lodged a report at 2.02am today, alleging that the incident occurred around 11.30am yesterday. He said initial investigations found that the woman was passing through a housing area when she encountered several workers appointed by the local council to conduct the stray animal operation.

items.title: Evocom IPO draws 3.6 times oversubscription
items.summary: Malaysian Issuing House Sdn Bhd said it received 6,326 applications for 104.69 million shares, against the 22.78 million new shares made available to local investors. The Bumiputera portion attracted 2,364 applications for 31.10 million shares, representing an oversubscription rate of 1.73 times. Meanwhile, the private placement of 34.17 million new shares to selected investors, 22 million existing shares offered by selling shareholders and 56.95 million new shares to selected Bumiputera investors have been fully placed.

items.title: Perdana Putra abuzz ahead of PH Presidential Council meeting
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Perdana Putra complex here came under close media attention today as the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council was set to meet amid heightened political developments surrounding Barisan Nasional's (BN) position in the unity government. The meeting, chaired by PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, is expected to discuss current political developments, including BN's position in the unity government. The meeting comes amid renewed political attention following the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under conditional house arrest, subject to a RM50 million fine.

items.title: Vestland secures RM107mil slope mitigation contract in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd announced that its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Vestland Infra Sdn Bhd had accepted a contract valued at RM107.61 million from Ambang Besar Sdn Bhd. Vestland joint managing director Datuk Seri Justin Soo Sze Ching noted that this project bolsters the group's infrastructure presence and highlights the ongoing expansion of its civil engineering portfolio. With this new project, Vestland has secured eight new contracts year-to-date with a combined value of RM1.6 billion, effectively lifting the group's total outstanding order book to RM2.0 billion.

items.title: Najib solidarity fund raises RM165,645 in first hour, says Umno sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Umno’s Najib Razak Solidarity Fund raised RM165,645 within its first hour of being launched today to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon, party secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said. “Alhamdulillah, within an hour of its launch, the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund has already reached RM165,645,” he wrote. The fundraising drive was launched after Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced today that the party would collect donations to help Najib pay the RM50 million fine.

items.title: Selangor mulls giving free reusable masks to students amid prolonged haze
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 18 — The Selangor state government is considering distributing free reusable cloth face masks to school students as the haze is expected to persist until October. Jamaliah said air quality was expected to improve over the next few days, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at moderate or good levels compared with last week. Six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy API readings this morning, with Johan Setia registering the highest reading at 196, followed by Shah Alam (171), Banting (166), Petaling Jaya (163), Klang (160) and Kuala Selangor (143).

items.title: From 1MDB appeal to billion-dollar civil claims: Najib’s legal battles continue despite conditional pardon
items.summary: The house-arrest arrangement concerns his six-year sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case, involving the misappropriation of RM42 million. The court ordered that the 15-year sentence would commence after Najib completes his sentence in the SRC International case. Najib filed an appeal against the conviction and sentence on December 29, 2025.

items.title: Handful of supporters wait outside Najib’s Langgak Duta residence after conditional pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Around 10 supporters gathered outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s private residence in Jalan Langgak Duta this afternoon, following news that he had been granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his custodial sentence under house arrest. The group arrived clad mostly in red, with one supporter wearing a red T-shirt featuring Najib’s portrait making a shushing gesture. Earlier today, the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department announced that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to grant Najib a conditional pardon, permitting him to serve out the rest of his term under home arrest until August 23, 2028, conditional upon the full settlement of an RM50 million fine.

items.title: Gold shop supervisor pawns RM176,200 in gold bars for cryptocurrency, gets 16 months’ jail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A former gold shop supervisor who pawned three gold bars to trade in cryptocurrency was sentenced to 16 months' jail and three strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court today for criminal breach of trust. He is also set to be sentenced on a separate criminal breach of trust charge over a pawned gold chain in another Sessions Court. The charges state that Koh, entrusted with three 999 gold bars weighing 50 grammes and 100 grammes, all worth RM176,200, pawned them at a pawnshop for his personal use.

items.title: MCA thanks King over Najib’s pardon, pledges to uphold constitutional supremacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — MCA has expressed its gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting a conditional royal pardon to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. In a statement today, MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said that honouring the Pardons Board’s decision does not negate the courts' earlier conviction of Najib, just as respecting judicial verdicts does not diminish the King’s constitutional prerogative to grant clemency. “MCA expresses our utmost gratitude for the royal assent granted by His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, regarding the conditional pardon of Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak,” Wee said.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: DAP leadership to decide party stance tomorrow, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — DAP will convene an emergency central executive committee (CEC) meeting tomorrow to decide its formal position in response to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, party secretary-general Anthony Loke announced today. Loke noted that the long-term financial fallout remains severe, citing recent Finance Ministry data indicating that 1MDB obligations have saddled taxpayers with RM51.4 billion in liabilities, comprising RM42.5 billion already settled and RM8.9 billion in outstanding debt. Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim maintained that the pardon does not dilute the government’s resolve to combat graft and power abuse.

items.title: ‘Thank you’: Negeri Sembilan ruler Tuanku Muhriz receives memorandum of loyalty
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Sept 18 — Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir today received a memorandum expressing loyalty and support for him after performing Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque here. Tuanku Muhriz was accompanied by his sons, Tunku Besar of Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin. After the prayers, Tuanku Muhriz received the memorandum from Dr Mohd Aluwi Sari, head of the Secretariat for Loyalty and Support for the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: PAS welcomes Najib house arrest, says he still has plenty to offer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — PAS today thanked His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon, saying he could still contribute his ideas and experience to the country. PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party was grateful for the King’s decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine. PAS also prayed that Najib would remain in good health while serving the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: Albert Tei fails in bid to move five corruption charges to High Court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The High Court today dismissed businessman Albert Tei’s application to transfer five corruption charges against him from the Sessions Court to the High Court. Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed the application by Tei, whose real name is Tei Jiann Cheing, 37, on the grounds that the issues raised were not complex and could be adequately dealt with in the Sessions Court. “I do not agree with the applicant’s (Tei) application.

items.title: Anwar: Najib house arrest does not weaken govt’s fight against corruption
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — The conditional pardon allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest does not weaken the government’s resolve to fight corruption and power abuse, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said all corruption cases, including ongoing proceedings involving Najib, must continue in accordance with the law. Anwar said Malaysia must remain firm in tackling corruption, with public support needed to ensure misconduct or abuse of power for personal enrichment is not taken lightly.

items.title: Teen driving Mercedes charged over crash that killed four family members in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Sept 18 — A 19-year-old student pursuing studies in Singapore was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with reckless and dangerous driving over a crash that killed four family members last June. Goh Yin Zun pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him through an interpreter before Magistrate Norasidah A Rahman, Berita Harian reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nik Noratini Nik Azam initially proposed bail at RM20,000.

items.title: Press swarm Kajang Prison and Langgak Duta after Najib’s pardon news
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 18 — Kajang Prison and the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak have become focal points for local and international media following the announcement that he has been granted a conditional pardon by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today. As of 12.30 pm, there was no movement involving the former prime minister detected at the Kajang Prison entrance. Najib, 73, has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022.

items.title: Zahid announces Umno donation drive to pay Najib’s RM50m fine following conditional pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Umno has launched a nationwide donation drive to assist former party president Datuk Seri Najib Razak in settling the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon, party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced today. Zahid said the party, representing its entire leadership and grassroots membership, conveyed its profound gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, describing the royal decision as a moment of tremendous relief for Najib, his family, and party loyalists who had “never ceased to hold hope and offer prayers” for his release. He also called on party members to welcome the royal decision with humility, decorum, and strict adherence to legal norms.

items.title: AGC rejects Zamri Vinoth’s bid to review charge over statement at KL rally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has rejected a representation by independent preacher Zamri Vinoth regarding a charge of making a statement likely to cause public alarm in connection with a gathering held in front of a shopping complex in the capital. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Farhana Mohamad Poad informed Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan of the decision during proceedings today. Lawyer Nur Shafiqah Shafiyah Omar, representing Zamri, subsequently requested that the court fix dates for the trial.

items.title: Haze update: 35 areas now with ‘Unhealthy’ API, Selangor’s Johan Setia tops 193
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further by midday today, with 35 monitoring stations recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 12pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data. Selangor followed closely with six stations recording elevated pollution. Alongside Johan Setia, unhealthy levels were logged in Shah Alam (172), Banting (166), Petaling Jaya (165), Klang (160), and Kuala Selangor (139).

items.title: Hannah Yeoh denies signing Najib house arrest order, calls document fake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has denied signing any house arrest order involving former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which has been circulating on social media. Hannah made the statement in a post on her X account early today. “I have never signed any house arrest order as claimed in the document.

items.title: Najib gets conditional pardon, to serve remainder of sentence under house arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has been granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, the Legal Affairs Division announced today. “His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia has consented to grant a conditional pardon to Datuk Seri Najib Razak, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until 23 August 2028, subject to his payment of a fine of RM50 million,” the statement said. The secretariat noted that Najib must strictly comply with all statutory terms attached to the royal pardon.

items.title: Malaysian Armed Forces plans special-needs child centres at major military camps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) aims to establish at least one Community Rehabilitation Centre (PPDK) at major camps to care for children with special needs. Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move is part of MAF's efforts to support its personnel, particularly those caring for special needs children. Meanwhile, Malek Razak said MAF is carrying out 898 maintenance projects involving 15,024 units of Armed Forces Family Housing (RKAT) to ensure comfortable living conditions for security force personnel.

items.title: Porsche driver surrenders after driving against traffic to flee Iskandar Puteri roadblock
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 18 — A 43-year-old local man has surrendered to the police after a viral video captured a white Porsche being driven against the flow of traffic to bypass a roadblock in Iskandar Puteri, Johor. In a statement on Thursday, Iskandar Puteri acting police chief Supt Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division detected the 12-second clip circulating on social media, which showed the sports car being driven recklessly through a police checkpoint at KM6.5 of Jalan Ismail Sultan. The driver turned himself in at the Iskandar Puteri District Police Headquarters on the same day the footage surfaced.

items.title: Officials depart as FT Pardons Board meeting concludes at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Vehicles carrying Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain were seen departing Istana Negara around 9.40am today following the conclusion of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting. The impromptu meeting has intensified public speculation that the board convened specifically to deliberate on the royal pardon petition of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which was deferred during the board's previous sitting on September 11. During that earlier meeting, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chairs the board, granted royal pardons to 65 other inmates while Najib's case was held back for further consideration.

items.title: Total standstill on NSE northbound after two box vans overturn near Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A crash involving two box vans that overturned on their sides has completely blocked all northbound lanes of the North-South Expressway (NSE) at KM257.7, along the stretch between the Menora Tunnel and Kuala Kangsar in Perak. The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) reported that northbound traffic ground to a complete standstill following the incident, triggering a 1.7km congestion queue as of 9.18am. Emergency response teams and recovery machinery are currently on-site working to clear the obstructed lanes.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar greeted by supporters at KLIA
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 18 — Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir expressed his appreciation for the support shown by over 200 members of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) who gathered at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 here last night to welcome his arrival. Asked if he would immediately resolve the Negeri Sembilan royal institution impasse, Tuanku Muhriz replied briefly: “Yes, insya-Allah , insya-Allah . More than 200 members of Negeri Sembilan non-governmental organisations gather to welcome Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1 in Sepang on September 17, 2026.

items.title: Police detain Chinese national after alleged theft attempt on Jakarta-Penang flight
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 18 — Police detained a Chinese national on suspicion of attempting to steal a passenger’s wallet during a flight from Jakarta, Indonesia, to Penang yesterday. Southwest district police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said police arrested the 55-year-old man at Penang International Airport after receiving a report from a 36-year-old Indonesian man about the incident. “During the flight, the Indonesian man saw the suspect remove his bag from the overhead compartment, open it and take his wallet.

items.title: Police sends probe papers on Umno delegate’s priest-nun comment to AGC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Police will submit the investigation papers on Selangor delegate Datuk Noorazli Said’s speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly on Sunday to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the case is classified under Section 298 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. According to him, police received 86 reports and recorded statements from 93 witnesses, including members of the public, organisers, Umno delegates and Noorazli.
